newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on world supplies, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on world supplies, funds.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on competition for U.S. export business amid increasing prospects for global wheat production, traders said.
"There are bigger wheat crops coming in all over the world and that's weighing on wheat. No one wants it right now," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders cited the Statistics Canada report early this week estimating Canada's wheat production this year at 29.84 million tonnes, up from trade expectations for 28.5 to 28.61 million tonnes.
Bright prospects for Australian wheat output also continued to limit gains in wheat futures, the traders said.
USDA's confirmation Wednesday that Egypt bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat was factored into the market Monday since the business was done over the weekend, they said.

Pressure also came from good harvest weather for the U.S. spring wheat crop and prospects for heavy deliveries to be posted against the September Friday, first notice day for deliveries on the September contracts.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 10-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down seven at $4.51-1/4.
Rosenthal Collins sold 3.5 million bushels of December. Farmers Commodities Corp sold 1.5 million December and The Chicago Corp sold 1.0 million bushels of December, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, up from 11,670 Tuesday.
In wheat options Refco Inc bought 100 December $4.70 calls, sold 100 December $5.00 calls and sold 100 December $4.40 puts at two cents.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000 contracts, up from 2,403 Tuesday.
